title: Investigation Facilitator Cheat Sheet and Escalation Flow
summary: Practical facilitator-centric runbook for coordinating an incident response across SRE, infra, product, and legal. Focuses on rapid evidence preservation, RBAC v2 action mapping for mitigations, SIEM extraction patterns, and templated comms for on-call ownership until handoff.
scope: Applies to security incidents that require live coordination (data exfiltration, privilege misuse, unusual RBAC changes, suspected SIEM alerts). Walkthrough assumes Redwood control plane + hosted & private deployments; includes vendor/export notes for on-prem collection.
facilitator_role: The Investigation Facilitator is the single point of contact for evidence collection and cross-team tasking during the first 6 hours of an incident. Responsibilities: maintain timeline, push preservation tasks, own evidence bag naming, and coordinate handoff to IR lead.
triage_matrix:
Severity decision matrix (quick):
- Critical: confirmed exfiltration, privileged key compromise, active lateral movement -> Pager, exec notify, IR lead engaged.
- High: anomalous RBAC grant, large audit-log deletion, persistent suspicious token -> Pager to security on-call + infra mute.
- Medium: single-user unexpected API misuse -> Slack to owner, ticket with monitoring.
- Low: benign alerts, false positives -> track in weekly review.
runbook_steps: 1) Initial intake (0-10m): Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty. Post incident header in #sec-incidents with short summary header, incident id, initial pager link, and facilitator name. Use template: 'INC-ID | short summary | owner: Aisha C. | severity: X | initial evidence: [link]'.

2) Quick containment (10-30m): If active abuse: rotate keys for impacted tokens (follow rotation playbook), block offending IP ranges at WAF, and apply temporary RBAC deny rule for the implicated role id. Note: make config change as 'temporary-mitigation/<INC-ID>' and record config diff in evidence bag.

3) Snapshot & preserve (15-45m): Kick off evidence collection tasks:
- Export control-plane audit logs for last 72 hours (use BQ export or /admin/audit/export endpoint).
- Snapshot instance disks (cloud snapshot or on-prem dd to secured host).
- Collect process list and netsstat on affected hosts.
- Pull Kubernetes audit logs and etcd revisions.
Naming convention: evidence/<INC-ID>/<collector>-<YYYYMMDD>-<sha256prefix>.tar.gpg

4) SIEM extraction (20-60m): Use provided SIEM queries to extract raw events and full message payloads. If SIEM export delay expected, request raw export from storage bucket. Preserve original event ids and include SIEM export manifest in evidence bag.

5) RBAC mapping & emergency role revocation (30-90m): Map user(s) to RBAC v2 role ids using 'rbac list' API, and stage emergency revocation via 'rbac revoke <role-id> --reason <INC-ID> --expires 1h'. Only escalate to org-wide role unbinding if evidence shows privilege misuse beyond single principal.

6) Forensic triage (1-6h): Coordinate with SRE and platform-engineering for memory/process dumps, forensic timeline (Rough timeline: initial compromise -> pivot -> exfil). Ensure chain-of-custody forms filled and hashes computed for each artifact.

7) External comms & legal (as needed): If data exposure possible, notify legal and privacy. Use templated packet that includes affected scopes, estimated user count, and mitigation steps. Do not share internal evidence until legal ok.

8) Handoff (4-12h): Create a formal handoff ticket to IR lead with evidence bag link, actions taken, outstanding tasks, and suggested next steps (forensic deep-dive, SIEM hunting, patching). Ensure two-person verification of all artifact hashes.

9) Post-incident follow-up (24-72h): Drive postmortem timeline creation, root cause hypotheses, and required product/security fixes. Add remediation owners and due dates to the postmortem template. Close the incident only after evidence retention policies are satisfied.
audit_query_templates: Splunk (RBAC change): index=audit source=controlplane action=role_update OR action=role_create user="*" | table _time, user, action, role_id, request_id | sort -_time
Elasticsearch (suspicious token): event.type:authentication AND event.outcome:failure AND user.name:* | sort @timestamp desc | limit 500

BigQuery (raw audit exports): SELECT timestamp, user_email, action, resource_name, payload FROM `redwood-prod.audit_logs` WHERE timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 3 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() AND (action LIKE '%role%' OR payload LIKE '%token%')
SIEM full payload pull: export events where event_id in (<comma list>) with originalRawEvent=true and include_http_headers=true. Always preserve event_id and sequence id in export manifest.
rbac_mappings: RBAC v2 quick map: role human name -> role_id examples: 'platform-admin' -> r2-0001b, 'service-deployer' -> r2-0034a, 'read-only-logs' -> r2-00f8c
Emergency deny pattern: use 'rbac policy add --principal <user-or-group> --deny --actions=all --note <INC-ID>' and tag with metadata 'temp=true;facilitator=<name>'.
Audit of RBAC changes: always call 'rbac history --role <role-id> --since 72h' and attach the CSV to evidence bag. Record the API call and response in the timeline.
evidence_collection_checklist: Create evidence bag directory: s3://redwood-sec-evidence/<INC-ID>/ (or on-prem NFS path if private) and set bucket/object ACL to security-team-only.
Export control-plane audit logs (full payload) and verify count matches SIEM export; include export manifest (file counts, sizes, sha256s).
Compute and record SHA256 for each artifact; store sha256s in evidence_manifest.txt signed by facilitator and one witness.
If disk images taken, preserve original VM metadata (instance id, zone, snapshot id) and attach cloud provider change log.
Collect network captures (pcap) limited to relevant time windows; redact unrelated private data; keep original copy sealed.
Document every action in timeline with username, command, timestamp, reason. Use ISO8601 with timezone.
siem_export_mapping:
recommended schema mapping -> field name:
- ingestion_time -> @timestamp
- principal -> user_email
- action_type -> action
- resource -> resource_name
- request_id -> request_id
- raw_payload -> payload.raw
store full JSON payloads as GZIP+NDJSON when exporting to S3; include manifest.json with event counts and first/last timestamps.
retention guidance: keep raw exports for minimum 90 days for high-severity incidents; aggregated logs can be reduced to 365 days per compliance rules.
automation_playbook: 1) Evidence export job (automated): Trigger on detection tag 'export-required' to run export-runner which: queries BQ/ES, writes ndjson to s3://redwood-sec-export/<INC-ID>/raw/ and generates manifest + sha256s.

2) Orchestration hook: automation should create ticket in /security/incidents with artifacts attached and notify facilitator via PagerDuty. Include pre-signed object links that expire in 7 days by default.

3) Hash verification lambda: after export, run verifier that recomputes and posts verification_status=true/false to evidence_manifest.json; if false, retry export up to 3 times and escalate to infra on-call.
4) Auto-redaction: run PII-scanner on raw payloads to create a redacted view for observers; original remains sealed for legal. Redaction report appended to manifest.
postmortem_template: Title: concise incident label (INC-ID + short desc)
Summary: 3-sentence executive summary: what happened, impact, mitigations
Timeline: bullet list ISO8601 events with actor and evidence link
Root cause analysis: hypothesis + evidence mapping (what changed, when, how)
Mitigations and follow-ups: owner, ETA, severity label
Lessons learned: process or tooling gaps discovered
Artifacts: link to evidence bag, SIEM export manifest, RBAC change CSV, forensic image checksums
notes: Facilitators should avoid making permanent RBAC removals—use timeboxed denies. For private deployments coordinate with customer ops to prevent accidental data export when pulling logs; always prefer server-side exports over client-side scraping. This doc is intentionally operational and meant to be referenced during live incidents; add local playbook links for cloud vendor-specific snapshot commands.
